question: What is the main reason student midwives do research presentations?

options.A: To bridge the gap between academic theory and clinical practice
options.B: To generate commercial revenue for the training institution
options.C: To replace traditional written examinations completely
options.D: To test the physical stamina of the graduating students

explanation: Research presentations help connect what is learned in textbooks to real-world challenges in maternal and child health. [learn more](BMP313_U1_T2#BMP313_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why do student midwives need to explain and defend their research methods?

options.A: To confuse the panel of senior clinical examiners
options.B: To prove their research is reliable and based on evidence
options.C: To avoid publishing the final study results
options.D: To show they spent a large amount of money

explanation: Defending methodology shows that the study was done properly and that the findings can be trusted to guide patient care. [learn more](BMP313_U1_T2#BMP313_U1_T2_h1)

question: Which part of a research proposal explains the exact gap in current clinical practice?
explanation: The problem statement points out what is missing or unknown in current practice, which justifies doing the research. [learn more](BMP313_U1_T2#BMP313_U1_T2_h2)

question: What information belongs in the methodology section of a proposal?

options.A: Personal reflections on the difficulty of writing
options.B: Broad political history of maternal health in Nigeria
options.C: Detailed biographies of all participating patients
options.D: Study design, population, and data collection tools

explanation: The methodology lays out the practical plan for how the study will be done, including who will be studied and how data will be gathered. [learn more](BMP313_U1_T2#BMP313_U1_T2_h2)

question: What is a common mistake when presenting preliminary study findings?

options.A: Using too many simple descriptive statistics
options.B: Discussing challenges faced during field data collection
options.C: Separating completed work from ongoing analysis
options.D: Overstating final conclusions from incomplete data

explanation: Since preliminary data is still partial, claiming absolute final results is misleading. [learn more](BMP313_U1_T2#BMP313_U1_T2_h3)

question: A student notices that data collection in the antenatal clinic is slower than expected. How should this be handled in a presentation?

options.A: Discuss it honestly as an ongoing fieldwork challenge
options.B: Pretend the sample size was reached successfully
options.C: Fabricate extra patient numbers to impress the panel
options.D: Omit the methodology section completely from the slides

explanation: Being transparent about field realities helps evaluators give useful feedback and realistic adjustments for the rest of the study. [learn more](BMP313_U1_T2#BMP313_U1_T2_h3)

question: What is the recommended minimum font size for body text on a presentation slide?
explanation: A font size of at least 24pt ensures that people sitting at the back of the room can easily read the text. [learn more](BMP313_U1_T2#BMP313_U1_T2_h4)

question: Why should students avoid putting heavy paragraphs of text on presentation slides?

options.A: It makes the projector bulb burn out faster
options.B: It prevents the use of any colors on the screen
options.C: It distracts the audience from listening to the speaker
options.D: It takes too much computer memory to save the file

explanation: When slides are packed with heavy text, the audience reads ahead instead of listening to the explanation. [learn more](BMP313_U1_T2#BMP313_U1_T2_h4)

question: Which practice helps a student keep a steady, conversational pace during a presentation?

options.A: Memorizing the entire presentation in a foreign language
options.B: Speaking as fast as possible to save time
options.D: Reading every slide word-for-word from a paper

explanation: Regular practice helps the speaker get comfortable with the flow, timing, and transitions without needing to rush. [learn more](BMP313_U1_T2#BMP313_U1_T2_h5)

question: What is the main danger of poor time management during an academic defense?

options.A: Making the room temperature rise noticeably
options.B: Causing the projector to overheat and shut down completely
options.C: Rushing through crucial conclusions and clinical recommendations
options.D: Forcing the audience to ask fewer questions at the end

explanation: Running out of time forces the student to skip the most important part of the study: what the findings mean for patient care. [learn more](BMP313_U1_T2#BMP313_U1_T2_h5)

question: How should a student respond when an examiner points out a valid limitation in their study?

options.A: Deny that the limitation exists in the data
options.B: Argue aggressively with the examiner to prove them wrong
options.C: Acknowledge it professionally and explain how to address it
options.D: Walk out of the lecture hall immediately in frustration

explanation: Accepting constructive criticism shows maturity and a commitment to producing good research. [learn more](BMP313_U1_T2#BMP313_U1_T2_h6)

question: Why is it important to stay calm and not get defensive during a critique session?

options.A: Because the session is being recorded for television broadcast
options.B: Because examiners will fail any student who speaks up
options.C: Because defense rules forbid students from talking back
options.D: Because feedback is meant to strengthen the research, not attack the student

explanation: Evaluators offer critiques to help refine the study design and improve the final academic output. [learn more](BMP313_U1_T2#BMP313_U1_T2_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT an acceptable practice when preparing research slides?

options.A: Citing literature sources correctly to avoid plagiarism
options.B: Acknowledging ethical approval from the hospital board
options.C: Removing personal identifiers to maintain patient confidentiality
options.D: Including real patient names and hospital numbers on slides

explanation: Patient confidentiality is essential; real names and hospital numbers must never be shown on public presentation slides. [learn more](BMP313_U1_T2#BMP313_U1_T2_h7)

question: Why must student researchers state their ethical approval status during a proposal presentation?

options.A: To guarantee that the research will be published abroad
options.B: To bypass the need for a methodology chapter
options.C: To prove the study protects human participants from harm
options.D: To show that they paid all required administrative fees

explanation: Ethical approval confirms that an institutional board has reviewed the study to ensure patient safety and rights are respected. [learn more](BMP313_U1_T2#BMP313_U1_T2_h7)
